Research Question

• What are the fundamental causes of the large
  differences in income per capita across countries?
• Better institutions: secure property rights, less
  distortionary policies -> more investment in
  physical and human capital
I. Why do we need IV?

Motivation

• Reverse causality: rich economies choose better
  institutions
• Omitted variable: economies that are different for a
  variety of reasons will differ both in their
  institutions and in their income per capita
• Measurement error: any measure only measures
  part of the institution, historical institution also
  matters, etc.


We need a source of exogenous variation in
institutions!
II. What is a good IV?
III. How to find a good IV?

How to find a good IV?

• IV is not omitted variable
• IV is an “exogenous” shock
• Sometimes, policy shocks, natural shocks or
  historical shocks are exogenous enough
• There is no definite rule – use your judgement!

Exogeneity

• Why not through health conditions?

IV. How to estimate a
model with IV?

V. How to test whether
an IV is good or not?

Exogeneity


Key Assumption: settler mortality in the past has no
direct effect on current economic performance


Test:
- Directly control for many of the variables that could
  plausibly be correlated with both settler mortality
 and economic outcomes, and checking whether the
  addition of these variables affects our estimate
- Overidentification test (caution: such tests may not
 lead to a rejection if all instruments are invalid, but
  still highly correlated with each other)
